---
title: "Education: autism in the school integration programme, special schools and the applications register"
subtitle: "PIE, SINACES and the JUNAEB school survey · 2019–2025 · annual school stocks, two definitions, one source switch and a survey whose weights arrive late"
---

```{python}
#| label: cargar-educacion
from pathlib import Path
import json
import sys
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats

ROOT = Path.cwd().parent if Path.cwd().name == "docs" else Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
from report_helpers import (show_table, kpis, note, number, ci, plot_style,
                            SEX_COLORS, COLORS)
from epi_helpers import count_ratio

# The education chapter reads only tracked tables: the tidy result tables in docs/study/data/ and
# the published corpus tables in docs/study/corpus/tables/. There is no shapefile dependency here,
# because no tracked education table carries a region or a commune.
DATA = ROOT / "docs" / "study" / "data"
CORPUS = ROOT / "docs" / "study" / "corpus" / "tables"


def read_data(name, **kwargs):
    return pd.read_csv(DATA / name, **kwargs)


def read_corpus(name, **kwargs):
    return pd.read_csv(CORPUS / name, **kwargs)


# Only the tables this chapter actually computes from are read. pie_enriched_context_verified.csv and
# fig3a_pie.csv are tracked restatements of education_summary_year.csv and of the provenance pivot built
# below; nothing on this page is derived from either, so neither is loaded or claimed as an input.
education = read_data("education_summary_year.csv")
provenance = read_data("pie_source_provenance.csv")
audit = read_data("junaeb_denominator_audit.csv")
coverage = read_data("coverage_layers_year.csv")
models = read_data("models_summary.csv", low_memory=False)
items = read_corpus("ST6_junaeb_items.csv")
pie_full = read_corpus("E76_education_pie_full.csv")
sex_levels = read_corpus("S12_junaeb_sex_level.csv")
controls = read_corpus("E79_reproduction_controls_by_family.csv")
plot_style()

# One wide frame of the provenance table: every published PIE/SINACES series by year, with the
# source document that carries it. Nothing below is typed in; each value is looked up here.
series = provenance.pivot_table(index="year", columns="series", values="value", aggfunc="first")
YEARS = [int(y) for y in education.year]
FIRST, LAST = min(YEARS), max(YEARS)
# OVERLAP_START: the first year the later document publishes a value at all.
# HANDOVER: the first year in which only the later document publishes it, so the series changes hands.
OVERLAP_START = int(provenance.loc[provenance.series.eq("pie_harmonised_sinaces"), "year"].min())
LAST_APUNTES = int(provenance.loc[provenance.series.eq("pie_harmonised_apuntes60"), "year"].max())
HANDOVER = LAST_APUNTES + 1
edu = education.set_index("year")
pop = coverage.set_index("year").ine_population_base2017_30jun

# JUNAEB, from wide to long: one row per school level and year.
LEVELS = {"parvularia": "Pre-school (NT1–NT2)", "basico1": "Grade 1 (1º básico)",
          "basico5": "Grade 5 (5º básico)", "medio1": "Grade 9 (1º medio)"}
LEVEL_ORDER = list(LEVELS.values())
ESTIMABLE = {"no": "No", "unweighted_only": "Unweighted only", "yes": "Yes, weighted"}
parts = []
for key, label in LEVELS.items():
    columns = {f"junaeb_{key}_n_students": "Students in the file",
               f"junaeb_{key}_tea_n": "Reported ASD (n)",
               f"junaeb_{key}_pct_weighted": "Weighted %",
               f"junaeb_{key}_pct_weighted_lo": "lo",
               f"junaeb_{key}_pct_weighted_hi": "hi",
               f"junaeb_{key}_pct_unweighted": "Unweighted %",
               f"junaeb_{key}_estimable": "Estimable"}
    part = education[["year"] + list(columns)].rename(columns=columns)
    part.insert(1, "Level", label)
    parts.append(part)
junaeb = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True).rename(columns={"year": "Year"})
junaeb["Estimable"] = junaeb.Estimable.map(ESTIMABLE)
LEVEL_KEYS = {label: key for key, label in LEVELS.items()}

# The survey's three timing facts — the first year the item exists at all, the year whose files carry no
# expansion weight, and the years in which a weighted estimate is possible — are read once from the
# tracked tables and reused wherever the chapter states them, so no year is typed into prose or caveat.
absent = items.loc[items["ASD variable"].eq("absent")]
ITEM_FIRST_YEAR = int(absent.Year.max()) + 1
unweighted_rows = np.isclose(audit.weighted_denominator_full, audit.n_total_raw)
NO_WEIGHT_YEAR = int(audit.loc[unweighted_rows, "year"].max())
WEIGHT_FIRST_YEAR = int(audit.loc[~unweighted_rows, "year"].min())
WEIGHTED_YEARS = sorted({int(y) for y in audit.loc[~unweighted_rows, "year"]})


def observed_codes(rows):
    """The ASD values actually present in the files of a survey year, blanks excluded."""
    codes = sorted({key for value in rows.item_observed_values for key in json.loads(value) if key != ""})
    return " and ".join(f"'{code}'" for code in codes) if codes else "none"


# Both PIE denominators move, and one of them collapses. The movements are computed once here so that
# every place the chapter prints a share can also print what the denominator of that share was doing.
enrolment = series["pie_total_enrolment"].dropna()
applicants = series["pie_total_applicants_sinaces"].dropna()
enrolment_change = 100 * enrolment.diff() / enrolment.shift()
applicants_change = 100 * applicants.diff() / applicants.shift()
DROP_YEAR = int(enrolment_change.idxmin())
REBOUND_YEAR = int(enrolment_change.idxmax())
share_of_enrolment = 100 * series["pie_harmonised"] / series["pie_total_enrolment"]
SHARE_RISE = float(share_of_enrolment[DROP_YEAR] - share_of_enrolment[DROP_YEAR - 1])
# Denominator contribution: the numerator held at its earlier value, divided by the new denominator.
SHARE_RISE_DENOMINATOR = float(100 * series.loc[DROP_YEAR - 1, "pie_harmonised"] / enrolment[DROP_YEAR]
                               - share_of_enrolment[DROP_YEAR - 1])
share_of_applicants = 100 * series["pie_harmonised"] / series["pie_total_applicants_sinaces"]
APPLICANT_DROP = float(applicants_change[LAST])
APPLICANT_SHARE_LAST = float(share_of_applicants[LAST])
# What the last share would read if its denominator had stayed where it was the year before.
APPLICANT_SHARE_HELD = float(100 * series.loc[LAST, "pie_harmonised"] / applicants[LAST - 1])

survey_tile = audit.loc[audit.year.eq(LAST) & audit.level.eq("parvularia")].iloc[0]
kpis([
    (number(series.loc[LAST, "pie_harmonised"]),
     f"Students with an autism category in the PIE register · {LAST} · annual stock of registrations, not persons"),
    (number(APPLICANT_SHARE_LAST, 1) + "%",
     f"Of the {number(series.loc[LAST, 'pie_total_applicants_sinaces'])} PIE applicants of every special educational "
     f"need · {LAST} · a denominator that fell {number(abs(APPLICANT_DROP), 1)}% from {LAST - 1}"),
    (number(series.loc[LAST, "special_schools_autism"]), f"Students in special autism schools · {LAST}"),
    (number(series.loc[LAST, "pie_tea_exceptional_entry"]), f"Autistic applicants entering by exceptional authorisation · {LAST}"),
    (number(edu.loc[LAST, "junaeb_parvularia_pct_weighted"], 1) + "%",
     f"Caregiver-reported ASD, pre-school school survey · {LAST} · weighted % of the "
     f"{number(survey_tile.n_total_raw)} records in the file "
     f"({ci(edu.loc[LAST, 'junaeb_parvularia_pct_weighted_lo'], edu.loc[LAST, 'junaeb_parvularia_pct_weighted_hi'], 1)}"
     ") · design inference not defensible; not central evidence"),
])
note(f"The first, third and fourth tiles are counts of school registrations in {LAST}: annual stocks of a register, "
     "not persons and not new cases. The second is a share whose denominator moves — total PIE applicants fell "
     f"{number(abs(APPLICANT_DROP), 1)}% between {LAST - 1} and {LAST} while the autism count rose, and "
     f"{number(APPLICANT_SHARE_LAST - APPLICANT_SHARE_HELD, 2)} of its {number(APPLICANT_SHARE_LAST, 1)} points is "
     "that fall rather than the numerator. The fifth is neither a count nor a rate: it is the weighted percentage of "
     f"the {number(survey_tile.n_total_raw)} pre-school records the JUNAEB school survey collected in {LAST}, "
     f"expanded by the published weight to {number(survey_tile.weighted_denominator_full)} and covering only the "
     "pre-school cohorts the survey reaches. The audit marks that exact cell design inference not defensible and not "
     "admissible as central evidence, because the file publishes no stratum, no primary sampling unit and no school "
     "identifier. A survey estimate and a register count are different quantities: they are not ordered against each "
     "other anywhere on this page, and none of the five tiles is a prevalence.")
```

## What the education records count

The education sources count **school registrations, not people diagnosed and not persons in the
population**. A student appears in the Programa de Integración Escolar (PIE, the school integration
programme) when a state-funded establishment registers that student under a permanent special
educational need and receives the associated subsidy; a student appears in the special-school series
when enrolled in an Escuela Especial de Autismo. Both are **annual stocks** of the school register:
one row per school year, never a count of new cases, never a count of unique persons across years,
and never a denominator-bearing rate. The JUNAEB school survey counts something different again — a
caregiver's answer to a checklist item in selected school cohorts. Nothing on this page is prevalence
or incidence; what rises here is administrative and educational recognition inside the school system.

```{python}
#| label: tabla-educacion-registros
# The caveats that carry a year are read from the tracked tables, not typed: the first year the item
# exists, the first year a weight is published, and the years in which the PIE denominator moves.
records = pd.DataFrame([
    {"Record": "PIE register (Apuntes 60)", "Unit of observation": "Student registered in PIE, by year",
     "What it counts": "Students with the permanent need \"Trastorno del Espectro Autista (P)\" and, separately, "
                       "\"Trastorno del Espectro Autista — Asperger (P)\"",
     "Caveat": "Published only as an aggregate; establishments in operation; no region, age or school breakdown. "
               f"Its denominator, total PIE enrolment, falls {number(abs(enrolment_change[DROP_YEAR]), 1)}% in "
               f"{DROP_YEAR} and rises {number(enrolment_change[REBOUND_YEAR], 1)}% in {REBOUND_YEAR}"},
    {"Record": "SINACES report (Law 21.545)", "Unit of observation": "Autistic student in the education system, by year",
     "What it counts": "PIE students, special-school students, their total, and PIE applicants by entry route",
     "Caveat": "Publishes the harmonised category only; no strict/Asperger split. Its denominator, total PIE "
               f"applicants, falls {number(abs(APPLICANT_DROP), 1)}% in {LAST}"},
    {"Record": "Special autism schools", "Unit of observation": "Student enrolled in a special school, by year",
     "What it counts": "Students in Escuelas Especiales de Autismo",
     "Caveat": "A separate provision, outside PIE, and included in the SINACES total"},
    {"Record": "JUNAEB EVE (school survey)", "Unit of observation": "Student record in selected cohorts",
     "What it counts": "Caregiver report of an ASD diagnosis, as one category of a prolonged-condition checklist",
     "Caveat": f"The item exists only from {ITEM_FIRST_YEAR}; expansion weights only from {WEIGHT_FIRST_YEAR}; "
               "strata, cluster and school identifier are never published"},
])
show_table(records, "What each education record counts, the unit it counts it in, and the caveat that travels with "
                    "every number taken from it")
```

The reading rules that follow from this are the ones the chapter applies throughout: the strict and
harmonised definitions are never mixed within a series; the Apuntes 60 and SINACES sources are
labelled wherever both exist; percentages are always accompanied by the denominator they were
divided by; and a cell that the source does not publish is reported as not published, never as zero.

## The programme: two definitions of the same spectrum

### The annual series

```{python}
#| label: tabla-pie-definiciones
table = pd.DataFrame({"Year": YEARS})
table["Strict autism (P)"] = table.Year.map(series["pie_tea_strict"])
table["Autism–Asperger (P)"] = table.Year.map(series["pie_tea_asperger"])
table["Harmonised (adopted)"] = table.Year.map(series["pie_harmonised"])
table["Harmonised, as printed by SINACES"] = table.Year.map(series["pie_harmonised_sinaces"])
table["Strict − harmonised check"] = (table["Strict autism (P)"] + table["Autism–Asperger (P)"]
                                      - table["Harmonised (adopted)"])
table["Total PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)"] = table.Year.map(series["pie_total_enrolment"])
table["Total PIE applicants (SINACES)"] = table.Year.map(series["pie_total_applicants_sinaces"])
table["Strict as % of PIE enrolment"] = 100 * table["Strict autism (P)"] / table["Total PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)"]
table["Harmonised as % of PIE enrolment"] = 100 * table["Harmonised (adopted)"] / table["Total PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)"]
table["Harmonised as % of PIE applicants"] = 100 * table["Harmonised (adopted)"] / table["Total PIE applicants (SINACES)"]
show_table(table, "PIE students with an autism category, by definition and by the denominator each share is taken over "
                  f"· {FIRST}–{LAST}. Counts are annual school-register stocks, not persons and not new cases",
           {c: 1 for c in table.columns if c.startswith(("Strict as", "Harmonised as"))})
note("The strict and Asperger categories sum exactly to the harmonised series in every year the split is published, "
     "which is what the check column shows. From "
     f"{HANDOVER} onward the split is not published at all, so the strict series simply stops: the harmonised "
     "series is the only one that runs the whole period. "
     "The three share columns carry a second warning, which belongs here and not in a closing list: their "
     f"denominators are not stable. Total PIE enrolment falls {number(abs(enrolment_change[DROP_YEAR]), 1)}% in "
     f"{DROP_YEAR} — from {number(enrolment[DROP_YEAR - 1])} to {number(enrolment[DROP_YEAR])} students of every "
     f"special educational need — and rises {number(enrolment_change[REBOUND_YEAR], 1)}% again in {REBOUND_YEAR}. Of "
     f"the {number(SHARE_RISE, 2)} percentage-point rise in the harmonised share between {DROP_YEAR - 1} and "
     f"{DROP_YEAR}, {number(SHARE_RISE_DENOMINATOR, 2)} points — {number(100 * SHARE_RISE_DENOMINATOR / SHARE_RISE)}% "
     "of it — is the denominator contracting, with the numerator held at its earlier value. Total PIE applicants "
     f"then falls {number(abs(APPLICANT_DROP), 1)}% in {LAST}. Every share on this page is read with the movement of "
     "its own denominator beside it.")
```

Two definitions coexist because the register itself carries two categories. **Strict autism** is the
permanent need labelled `Trastorno del Espectro Autista (P)`; **Autism–Asperger** is a separate
permanent need kept from the pre-DSM-5 nomenclature. Reporting only the strict category would drop
every student registered under the older label; reporting only their sum would hide that the two
categories behave very differently. Both are therefore reported, and the harmonised series — their
sum — is the one used wherever a single number is needed, because it is the only definition the
later source publishes.

```{python}
#| label: fig-pie-definiciones

All counts are annual school-register stocks. The dotted line marks the year the categorical split stops being published; the dash-dotted lines mark the years in which the denominator of the share itself moves sharply."
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 4.2
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 4.2), layout="constrained")
strict = series["pie_tea_strict"].dropna()
asperger = series["pie_tea_asperger"].dropna()
harmonised = series["pie_harmonised"].dropna()
axes[0].plot(harmonised.index, harmonised.values, "o-", color=COLORS[0], label="Harmonised (strict + Asperger)")
axes[0].plot(strict.index, strict.values, "s--", color=COLORS[1], label="Strict autism (P)")
axes[0].plot(asperger.index, asperger.values, "^--", color=COLORS[2], label="Autism–Asperger (P)")
axes[0].axvline(HANDOVER - 0.5, color="#999999", linestyle=":", linewidth=1)
axes[0].annotate("split no longer\npublished", (HANDOVER - 0.45, axes[0].get_ylim()[1] * 0.35), fontsize=7, color="#555555")
axes[0].set(title="Students registered, by definition", xlabel="School year", ylabel="Students", xticks=YEARS)
axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
shares = pd.DataFrame({
    "Strict autism": 100 * series["pie_tea_strict"] / series["pie_total_enrolment"],
    "Autism–Asperger": 100 * series["pie_tea_asperger"] / series["pie_total_enrolment"],

axes[1].plot(shares.index, shares["Strict autism"], "s-", color=COLORS[1], label="Strict autism (P)")
axes[1].plot(shares.index, shares["Autism–Asperger"], "^-", color=COLORS[2], label="Autism–Asperger (P)")

            xticks=[y for y in YEARS if y <= LAST_APUNTES])
axes[1].legend(fontsize=8)
denominators = pd.DataFrame({
    "% of PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)": 100 * series["pie_harmonised"] / series["pie_total_enrolment"],
    "% of PIE applicants (SINACES)": 100 * series["pie_harmonised"] / series["pie_total_applicants_sinaces"],
})
axes[2].plot(denominators.index, denominators["% of PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)"], "o-", color=COLORS[0],
             label="÷ PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)")
axes[2].plot(denominators.index, denominators["% of PIE applicants (SINACES)"], "D--", color=COLORS[4],
             label="÷ PIE applicants (SINACES)")
# Both denominators of this panel move against the numerator: enrolment collapses in DROP_YEAR, and
# applicants fall in the final year. Both are marked here, beside the shares they move.
axes[2].axvline(DROP_YEAR, color="#b3271e", linestyle="-.", linewidth=1.1)
axes[2].annotate(f"PIE enrolment {number(enrolment_change[DROP_YEAR], 1)}%", (DROP_YEAR + 0.08, 0.80), fontsize=6.5,
                 color="#b3271e", xycoords=axes[2].get_xaxis_transform())
axes[2].axvline(LAST, color="#b3271e", linestyle="-.", linewidth=1.1)
axes[2].annotate(f"PIE applicants {number(APPLICANT_DROP, 1)}%", (LAST - 0.08, 0.80), ha="right", fontsize=6.5,
                 color="#b3271e", xycoords=axes[2].get_xaxis_transform())
axes[2].set(title="Harmonised series, two denominators", xlabel="School year", ylabel="% of the denominator", xticks=YEARS)
axes[2].legend(fontsize=8)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: tabla-pie-definiciones-crecimiento
pie_models = models.loc[models.estimand == "est_pie"].copy()
LABELS = {"pie_harmonised": "Harmonised (strict + Asperger)", "pie_tea_strict_n": "Strict autism (P)",
          "pie_tea_asperger_n": "Autism–Asperger (P)"}

pie_models["Series"] = pie_models.model_id.str.split(":").str[0].map(LABELS)
pie_models["Adjustment"] = pie_models.model_id.str.split(":").str[1].map(COVARIATES)

show_table(pie_models[["Series", "years", "Adjustment", "n_obs", "df_resid", "apc", "95% CI", "p_value",
                       "dispersion", "durbin_watson"]].rename(columns={
    "years": "Years", "n_obs": "Points", "df_resid": "Residual df", "apc": "AAPC (%)", "p_value": "p value",
    "dispersion": "Dispersion", "durbin_watson": "Durbin–Watson"}),
    "Average annual percent change of the PIE series (log-linear quasi-Poisson on the annual stock, as computed in "
    "models_summary.csv). The dispersion and Durbin–Watson columns are the reason these intervals are read as "
    "descriptive: with fewer than eight points the autocorrelation statistic is indicative only",
    {"AAPC (%)": 1, "p value": 4, "Dispersion": 1, "Durbin–Watson": 2})
strict_model = pie_models.loc[pie_models.model_id.eq(f"pie_tea_strict_n:none:{FIRST}-{LAST_APUNTES}")].iloc[0]
asperger_model = pie_models.loc[pie_models.model_id.eq(f"pie_tea_asperger_n:none:{FIRST}-{LAST_APUNTES}")].iloc[0]
note(f"Over {FIRST}–{LAST_APUNTES}, the years in which both categories are published, strict autism grows at "
     f"{number(strict_model.apc, 1)}% a year ({ci(strict_model.apc_lo, strict_model.apc_hi)}) and Autism–Asperger at "
     f"{number(asperger_model.apc, 1)}% ({ci(asperger_model.apc_lo, asperger_model.apc_hi)}). "
     "The two definitions therefore do not merely differ in level: they move at different speeds, which is why a "
     "series built from one of them cannot be spliced onto a series built from the other. None of these models "
     "estimates an effect of any policy; they are descriptive log-linear slopes on an administrative stock.")
```

The strict category multiplies several times over while the Asperger category grows slowly, so the
composition of the harmonised series changes from year to year. In practice this is a coding
migration inside the register: establishments increasingly register students under the DSM-5-aligned
label rather than the older one. Reading the strict series alone would overstate the change in
recognition; reading the Asperger series alone would understate it.

## The source switch, and what it does to comparability

### What the provenance table records

```{python}
#| label: tabla-pie-procedencia
# The provenance file records each definition in the language of the source document; the published
# corpus table E76 carries the English definition of the same series, and is used for display.
# E76 carries one English definition per published series, but `pie_harmonised` is published by two
# documents under two different definitions, so the definition has to be resolved per (series, document)
# and not per series: mapping by series alone printed the Apuntes 60 definition against the SINACES years.
# When a series' own E76 row cites more than one document, the definition is taken from the source-specific
# sibling row — the shortest series name extending it whose Source cites this document and no other.
def english_definition(series_name, source_file):
    exact = pie_full.loc[pie_full.Series.eq(series_name)]
    if len(exact) and exact.Source.iloc[0].count(".pdf") == 1:
        return exact.Definition.iloc[0]
    siblings = pie_full.loc[pie_full.Series.str.startswith(series_name + "_")
                            & pie_full.Source.str.contains(source_file, regex=False)
                            & pie_full.Source.str.count(r"\.pdf").eq(1)]
    if len(siblings):
        return siblings.loc[siblings.Series.str.len().idxmin(), "Definition"]
    return exact.Definition.iloc[0] if len(exact) else np.nan

prov = provenance.groupby(["series", "source_file", "pdf_page", "table_or_figure_caption", "derived"],
                          dropna=False).agg(**{
    "First year": ("year", "min"), "Last year": ("year", "max"), "Years": ("year", "size"),
    "SHA-256 (first 12)": ("source_sha256", lambda s: s.iloc[0][:12])}).reset_index()
prov["Definition"] = [english_definition(s, f) for s, f in zip(prov.series, prov.source_file)]
prov["Derived"] = np.where(prov.derived, "computed from published cells", "printed in the document")
prov = prov.sort_values(["source_file", "series"])
# "First year"/"Last year" are years, not quantities: kept as text so they print 2019, not 2,019.
for column in ("First year", "Last year"):
    prov[column] = prov[column].astype(int).astype(str)
show_table(prov[["series", "source_file", "pdf_page", "table_or_figure_caption", "Definition",
                 "First year", "Last year", "Years", "Derived", "SHA-256 (first 12)"]].rename(columns={
    "series": "Series", "source_file": "Source document", "pdf_page": "Page",
    "table_or_figure_caption": "Table in the document (caption verbatim)"}),
    "Provenance of every published PIE, SINACES and special-school value: the document, the page, the table whose "
    "caption is quoted as printed, the definition of the series, and whether the value is printed in the document or "
    "computed from cells that are")
documents = provenance.groupby("source_file").agg(
    n_series=("series", "nunique"), n_values=("value", "size"),
    first=("year", "min"), last=("year", "max")).reset_index()
note("Three documents carry the whole education series: " + "; ".join(
    f"{row.source_file} ({row.n_series} series, {row.n_values} values, {int(row.first)}–{int(row.last)})"
    for row in documents.itertuples()) + ". Each value keeps its page, its table caption and the SHA-256 of the "
    "file it was read from, so any figure on this page can be traced back to a page of a specific document.")
```

### Where the series changes hands

```{python}
#| label: tabla-pie-cambio-fuente
both = series[["pie_harmonised_apuntes60", "pie_harmonised_sinaces"]].dropna(how="all").copy()
both["Difference (SINACES − Apuntes 60)"] = both.pie_harmonised_sinaces - both.pie_harmonised_apuntes60
both["Relative difference (%)"] = 100 * both["Difference (SINACES − Apuntes 60)"] / both.pie_harmonised_apuntes60
both["Adopted value"] = both.index.map(series["pie_harmonised"])
both["Source adopted"] = both.index.map(education.set_index("year").pie_harmonised_source)
show_table(both.reset_index().rename(columns={
    "year": "Year", "pie_harmonised_apuntes60": "Apuntes 60 (sum of the two categories)",
    "pie_harmonised_sinaces": "SINACES (as printed)"}),
    "The years in which both sources publish the harmonised series, the years in which only one does, and the value "
    "the study adopts in each", {"Relative difference (%)": 3})
overlap = both.dropna(subset=["pie_harmonised_apuntes60", "pie_harmonised_sinaces"])
gap_years = overlap.loc[overlap["Difference (SINACES − Apuntes 60)"] != 0]
note(f"The two sources overlap in {len(overlap)} years. They agree exactly in "
     f"{len(overlap) - len(gap_years)} of them. In "
     + ", ".join(f"{int(y)} they differ by {number(abs(v))} students ({number(abs(p), 2)}% of the Apuntes 60 value)"
                 for y, v, p in zip(gap_years.index, gap_years["Difference (SINACES − Apuntes 60)"],
                                    gap_years["Relative difference (%)"])) + ". "
     "The study adopts the Apuntes 60 value in the overlap because it is the disaggregated source — it publishes the "
     "two categories that make up the sum — and because the SINACES total minus its own special-school count "
     "reproduces it exactly. The printed SINACES figure is kept in its own series rather than discarded.")
```

Right: the SINACES arithmetic — the published total of autistic students in the education system, the special-school students it contains, and the PIE remainder that should equal the harmonised series."


The series changes hands between the two documents, and that is a break in the record, not in the
phenomenon. Apuntes 60 publishes the two categories separately for the earlier years and stops;
SINACES publishes only the harmonised category and only from the later years. The overlap is what
makes the splice defensible: in the years both documents cover, they agree to within a handful of
students out of tens of thousands. But three things still change at the switch, and they should be
carried with every number after it. The categorical split disappears, so the strict and Asperger
series cannot be continued. The denominator changes from **total PIE enrolment** to **total PIE
applicants**. And the documents' rounding conventions differ from the computed shares, which is why
the published percentages and the ones recomputed here are not identical to the last digit.

```{python}
#| label: tabla-pie-porcentajes-publicados
published = pd.DataFrame({"Year": YEARS})
published["Strict, % published"] = published.Year.map(series["pie_tea_strict_share_of_pie_pct_published"])
published["Strict, % recomputed"] = published.Year.map(series["pie_tea_strict_share_of_pie_pct"])
published["Asperger, % published"] = published.Year.map(series["pie_tea_asperger_share_of_pie_pct_published"])
published["Autism applicants, % published"] = published.Year.map(series["pie_tea_share_of_applicants_published_pct"])
published["Autism applicants, % recomputed"] = published.Year.map(series["pie_tea_share_of_applicants_pct"])
published["Largest absolute gap (pp)"] = np.nanmax(np.abs(np.c_[
    published["Strict, % published"] - published["Strict, % recomputed"],
    published["Autism applicants, % published"] - published["Autism applicants, % recomputed"]]), axis=1)
show_table(published, "Percentages as printed in the documents and as recomputed from the counts they publish; the "
                      "gaps are rounding in the printed tables, not a disagreement about the counts",
           {c: 3 for c in published.columns if c != "Year"})
edu_controls = controls.loc[controls.Module.eq("05_education")]
note(f"The education module carries {int(pd.to_numeric(edu_controls.Checks).sum())} reproduction controls across "
     f"{len(edu_controls)} families; {int(pd.to_numeric(edu_controls.Reproduced).sum())} reproduce and "
     f"{int(edu_controls.Differ.sum())} differ. The largest relative difference in any of them, "
     f"{number(pd.to_numeric(edu_controls['Max |relative difference|'], errors='coerce').max(), 4)}, comes from the "
     "published-versus-recomputed percentage families above and reflects the documents' rounding.")
```

## Denominators: enrolment, applicants, and the population behind neither

```{python}
#| label: tabla-pie-denominadores
den = pd.DataFrame({"Year": YEARS})
den["Total PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)"] = den.Year.map(series["pie_total_enrolment"])
den["Enrolment, change on the year (%)"] = den.Year.map(enrolment_change)
den["Total PIE applicants (SINACES)"] = den.Year.map(series["pie_total_applicants_sinaces"])
den["Applicants, change on the year (%)"] = den.Year.map(applicants_change)
den["Applicants − enrolment"] = den["Total PIE applicants (SINACES)"] - den["Total PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)"]
den["Harmonised autism students"] = den.Year.map(series["pie_harmonised"])
den["INE resident population (30 June)"] = den.Year.map(pop)
den["Per 100 000 residents of all ages"] = 1e5 * den["Harmonised autism students"] / den["INE resident population (30 June)"]
show_table(den, "The denominators the education series can be divided by, and the one it cannot. The last column is a "
                "context ratio only: its numerator is a school registration and its denominator is the whole "
                "resident population of every age, so it is not a rate of anything",
           {"Per 100 000 residents of all ages": 1, "Enrolment, change on the year (%)": 1,
            "Applicants, change on the year (%)": 1})
common = den.dropna(subset=["Total PIE enrolment (Apuntes 60)", "Total PIE applicants (SINACES)"])
note(f"Neither denominator is a fixed base. Total PIE enrolment falls {number(abs(enrolment_change[DROP_YEAR]), 1)}% "
     f"in {DROP_YEAR} and rebounds {number(enrolment_change[REBOUND_YEAR], 1)}% in {REBOUND_YEAR}, which is why the "
     f"share of PIE enrolment rises {number(SHARE_RISE, 2)} points in {DROP_YEAR} with "
     f"{number(SHARE_RISE_DENOMINATOR, 2)} of those points coming from the denominator alone; total PIE applicants "
     f"falls {number(abs(APPLICANT_DROP), 1)}% in {LAST} while the autism count rises. The "
     f"{FIRST + 1}–{FIRST + 2} reporting-disruption indicator used in the growth models above is applied to the "
     "counts, not to these shares: a share whose denominator moved cannot be repaired by an indicator on the "
     "numerator's trend.")
note("In the years both are published, SINACES's total of PIE applicants and Apuntes 60's total of PIE enrolment "
     "differ by " + ", ".join(f"{number(abs(d))} in {int(y)}" for y, d in
                              zip(common.Year, common["Applicants − enrolment"])) + ". "
     "The same is true of the autism numerator: SINACES's count of autistic PIE applicants equals its own count of "
     "autistic students in PIE in every year it publishes both. In this source, therefore, applying and being "
     "registered are not distinguished; the applicants table is a re-presentation of the enrolment table, not an "
     "independent measure of demand.")
```

The third denominator, the resident population, is shown once and then left alone. A school
registration divided by the population of every age is not an educational rate, not a prevalence and
not comparable with the health-record rates elsewhere in this report, which have residents as both
unit and denominator. It appears here only so that the order of magnitude of the school series can be
placed beside the other sources, and it carries the same warning wherever it is used.

## Applications: regular and exceptional entry

```{python}
#| label: tabla-pie-postulaciones
entry = pd.DataFrame({"Year": [y for y in YEARS if not np.isnan(series["pie_tea_applicants_sinaces"].get(y, np.nan))]})
entry["Autistic applicants"] = entry.Year.map(series["pie_tea_applicants_sinaces"])
entry["Regular entry (Decree 170 places)"] = entry.Year.map(series["pie_tea_regular_entry"])
entry["Exceptional entry (Seremi authorisation)"] = entry.Year.map(series["pie_tea_exceptional_entry"])
entry["Regular + exceptional check"] = (entry["Regular entry (Decree 170 places)"]
                                        + entry["Exceptional entry (Seremi authorisation)"]
                                        - entry["Autistic applicants"])
entry["% by exceptional entry"] = 100 * entry["Exceptional entry (Seremi authorisation)"] / entry["Autistic applicants"]
entry["All PIE applicants"] = entry.Year.map(series["pie_total_applicants_sinaces"])
entry["Autistic applicants as % of all"] = 100 * entry["Autistic applicants"] / entry["All PIE applicants"]
show_table(entry, "Autistic PIE applicants by entry route. The check column confirms that the two routes exhaust the "
                  "total in every year; percentages are of the autistic applicants and of all applicants respectively",
           {"% by exceptional entry": 1, "Autistic applicants as % of all": 1})
first_entry, last_entry = entry.iloc[0], entry.iloc[-1]
previous_entry = entry.iloc[-2]
# What the final share would read if its denominator had stayed at the previous year's value.
share_held = 100 * last_entry["Autistic applicants"] / previous_entry["All PIE applicants"]
denominator_fall = 100 * (last_entry["All PIE applicants"] / previous_entry["All PIE applicants"] - 1)
numerator_rise = 100 * (last_entry["Autistic applicants"] / previous_entry["Autistic applicants"] - 1)
note(f"Exceptional entry — the route requiring a regional authorisation because the establishment's Decree 170 "
     f"places are already taken — rises from {number(first_entry['% by exceptional entry'], 1)}% of autistic "
     f"applicants in {int(first_entry.Year)} to {number(last_entry['% by exceptional entry'], 1)}% in "
     f"{int(last_entry.Year)}. Over the same years the total of all PIE applicants moves from "
     f"{number(first_entry['All PIE applicants'])} to {number(last_entry['All PIE applicants'])}, and it does not "
     f"move in one direction: between {int(previous_entry.Year)} and {int(last_entry.Year)} it falls "
     f"{number(abs(denominator_fall), 1)}%, from {number(previous_entry['All PIE applicants'])} to "
     f"{number(last_entry['All PIE applicants'])}, while the autistic numerator rises {number(numerator_rise, 1)}%. "
     f"Of the {number(last_entry['Autistic applicants as % of all'], 1)}% the autism share reaches in "
     f"{int(last_entry.Year)}, {number(last_entry['Autistic applicants as % of all'] - share_held, 2)} points are "
     f"the denominator shrinking: the same numerator over the {int(previous_entry.Year)} denominator would read "
     f"{number(share_held, 1)}%. Part of the rise in the share is a numerator effect, and part is a denominator "
     "that shrinks beneath it.")
```

```{python}
sexes = pd.DataFrame(rows)

     "registration is differently distributed between girls and boys.")
```

## The school survey: what a caregiver checklist can carry

The Encuesta de Vulnerabilidad Estudiantil (EVE), the annual school-feeding and vulnerability survey
run by JUNAEB, is the only education source in this study with a student-level record. It is also the
one whose weaknesses need stating most carefully, because it is the only one that looks like it could
produce a prevalence estimate — and it cannot.

### The item, and the years it did not exist

```{python}
#| label: tabla-junaeb-items
item_table = items[["Year", "Level", "ASD variable", "Observed ASD codes", "Filter variable",
                    "Auxiliary variables (weight · sex · grade)", "Other item categories (n)", "Estimability"]].copy()
item_table["Weight column"] = item_table["Auxiliary variables (weight · sex · grade)"].str.split(" · ").str[0]
show_table(item_table[["Year", "Level", "ASD variable", "Observed ASD codes", "Filter variable", "Weight column",
                       "Other item categories (n)", "Estimability"]],
           "The ASD item in the school survey, year by year and level by level: the variable that carries it, the "
           "values actually observed in the file, the filter question that gates it, and the weight column the file "
           "publishes. Variable names, response codes and question wording change every year")
note(f"In {absent.Year.min()}–{absent.Year.max()} the questionnaire has no autism category at all: "
     f"{len(absent)} level-years in which the prolonged-condition checklist lists asthma, epilepsy, obesity, coeliac "
     "disease and the rest but not autism. Those years are not zeros and not low values; the question was never "
     "asked. The variable name changes in every year it does exist, the response codes change from a single letter "
     "to a word to a 0/1 pair, and the filter question is reworded more than once. There is no single extraction "
     "rule that works across years.")
```

### Weights, and the year they were missing

```{python}
#| label: tabla-junaeb-pesos
weights = audit[["year", "level", "n_total_raw", "n_weight_present_positive", "n_weight_missing",
                 "weighted_denominator_full", "design_inference_defensible", "include_in_central_evidence"]].copy()
weights["Level"] = weights.level.map({k: v for k, v in LEVELS.items()})
weights["Expansion factor (weighted ÷ raw)"] = weights.weighted_denominator_full / weights.n_total_raw
weights["Rows with no usable weight"] = weights.n_weight_missing
weights["Design inference defensible"] = np.where(weights.design_inference_defensible, "yes", "no")
weights["Used as central evidence"] = np.where(weights.include_in_central_evidence, "yes", "no")
show_table(weights.sort_values(["year", "Level"])[[
    "year", "Level", "n_total_raw", "weighted_denominator_full", "Expansion factor (weighted ÷ raw)",
    "Rows with no usable weight", "Design inference defensible", "Used as central evidence"]].rename(columns={
    "year": "Year", "n_total_raw": "Records in the file", "weighted_denominator_full": "Weighted denominator"}),
    "Weights in the survey files. An expansion factor of exactly 1 means no weight was published and the audit used "
    "unit weights for arithmetic only", {"Weighted denominator": 0, "Expansion factor (weighted ÷ raw)": 3})
weighted_factors = weights.loc[~unweighted_rows, "Expansion factor (weighted ÷ raw)"]
note(f"In {NO_WEIGHT_YEAR} the files carry no expansion factor, so no national figure can be produced from that "
     "year at all: what is reported is an unweighted proportion of the records in the file, with a Wilson interval, "
     "and it is not comparable with the weighted years that follow. From "
     f"{WEIGHT_FIRST_YEAR} the weight column exists and is verified, and the weighted denominator exceeds the raw "
     f"record count by a factor of {number(weighted_factors.min(), 3)} to {number(weighted_factors.max(), 3)}. "
     "But the audit marks design inference as not defensible in every single level-year, including the weighted "
     "ones, because the published files contain no stratum, no primary sampling unit and no school identifier: the "
     "standard errors below treat students as independent, which ignores clustering within schools and is therefore "
     "optimistic. None of these level-years is used as central evidence anywhere in the study.")
```

### Missingness, and the three denominators it creates

```{python}
#| label: tabla-junaeb-denominadores
den_audit = audit.copy()
den_audit["Level"] = den_audit.level.map(LEVELS)
den_audit["Answered the filter"] = den_audit.n_filter_yesno_all
den_audit["Said yes, left the checklist blank"] = den_audit.n_item_blank_filter_yes
den_audit["Complete case"] = den_audit.n_explicit_outcome_complete_case
den_audit["% of filter answers lost to the complete case"] = 100 * (
    den_audit.n_filter_yesno_all - den_audit.n_explicit_outcome_complete_case) / den_audit.n_filter_yesno_all
den_audit["Full-file %"] = den_audit.weighted_pct_full
den_audit["Filter-valid %"] = den_audit.weighted_pct_filter_valid
den_audit["Complete-case %"] = den_audit.weighted_pct_complete_case
den_audit["Spread, full to complete case (pp)"] = den_audit["Complete-case %"] - den_audit["Full-file %"]
show_table(den_audit.sort_values(["year", "Level"])[[
    "year", "Level", "n_total_raw", "Answered the filter", "Said yes, left the checklist blank", "Complete case",
    "% of filter answers lost to the complete case", "Full-file %", "Filter-valid %", "Complete-case %",
    "Spread, full to complete case (pp)"]].rename(columns={
    "year": "Year", "n_total_raw": "Records in the file"}),
    "One numerator, three defensible denominators. The published estimate uses the full file; restricting to the "
    "students whose caregiver answered the filter raises it; restricting further to students with an explicit answer "
    "on the checklist raises it much more",
    {c: 2 for c in ["% of filter answers lost to the complete case", "Full-file %", "Filter-valid %",
                    "Complete-case %", "Spread, full to complete case (pp)"]})
estimable_rows = den_audit.dropna(subset=["Full-file %"])
worst = estimable_rows.loc[estimable_rows["Spread, full to complete case (pp)"].idxmax()]
interval_width = float(edu.loc[int(worst.year), f"junaeb_{worst.level}_pct_weighted_hi"]
                       - edu.loc[int(worst.year), f"junaeb_{worst.level}_pct_weighted_lo"]) \
    if not pd.isna(edu.loc[int(worst.year), f"junaeb_{worst.level}_pct_weighted"]) else float("nan")
note(f"The widest case is {worst.Level} in {int(worst.year)}: "
     f"{number(worst['Said yes, left the checklist blank'])} students whose caregiver reported a prolonged condition "
     "left every checklist category blank, which is "
     f"{number(worst['% of filter answers lost to the complete case'], 1)}% of everyone who answered the filter. "
     f"Moving from the full file to the complete case shifts the estimate by "
     f"{number(worst['Spread, full to complete case (pp)'], 2)} percentage points"
     + (f", against a 95% interval {number(interval_width, 2)} points wide." if np.isfinite(interval_width) else ".")
     + " In that year the choice of denominator moves the answer by far more than sampling error does, and no "
       "assumption about those blank checklists is testable from the file.")
final_rows = den_audit.loc[den_audit.year.eq(LAST)]
previous_rows = den_audit.loc[den_audit.year.eq(LAST - 1)]
# "Coded 0/1 for every respondent" would be wrong: the checklist is coded for everyone who reaches it,
# and most records never reach it because their caregiver did not answer yes at the filter question.
reached = int(final_rows.n_item_nonempty.sum())
never_reached = int((final_rows.n_total_raw - final_rows.n_item_nonempty).sum())
note(f"The instrument changes in {LAST}, but not as far as it first appears. The checklist categories carry an "
     f"explicit 0 or 1 for every respondent who reaches them — every caregiver who answered yes at the filter — so "
     f"the students who reported a prolonged condition and then left the checklist blank fall from "
     f"{number(previous_rows['Said yes, left the checklist blank'].sum())} in {LAST - 1} to "
     f"{number(final_rows['Said yes, left the checklist blank'].sum())}, and the filter-valid and complete-case "
     f"denominators coincide exactly. The item itself is still empty in most records: of the "
     f"{number(int(final_rows.n_total_raw.sum()))} records collected in {LAST}, only {number(reached)} carry a 0 or "
     f"a 1 and {number(never_reached)} are blank, because their caregiver never answered yes at the filter and was "
     "never shown the list. The full file "
     "therefore remains a third and different denominator even in the year the instrument was fixed, and the fix "
     "arrives only for the last year of the series.")
```

```{python}
#| label: tabla-junaeb-sexo
counts = sex_levels.copy()
for source, target in [("Students with a response (n)", "n"), ("Reported ASD (n)", "x")]:
    counts[target] = pd.to_numeric(counts[source].astype(str).str.replace(",", "", regex=False), errors="coerce")
wide = counts.pivot_table(index=["Year", "Level"], columns="Sex", values=["n", "x"])
rows = []
z = stats.norm.ppf(0.975)
for (year, level), row in wide.iterrows():
    n_m, n_f = row.get(("n", "Males"), np.nan), row.get(("n", "Females"), np.nan)
    x_m, x_f = row.get(("x", "Males"), np.nan), row.get(("x", "Females"), np.nan)
    if not np.isfinite([n_m, n_f, x_m, x_f]).all() or min(x_m, x_f) <= 0:
        continue
    p_m, p_f = x_m / n_m, x_f / n_f
    se = np.sqrt((1 - p_m) / x_m + (1 - p_f) / x_f)
    ratio = p_m / p_f
    rows.append({"Year": year, "Level": level, "Males with a response": n_m, "Reported ASD, males": x_m,
                 "% males": 100 * p_m, "Females with a response": n_f, "Reported ASD, females": x_f,
                 "% females": 100 * p_f, "Ratio of the two percentages": ratio,
                 "95% CI": ci(ratio * np.exp(-z * se), ratio * np.exp(z * se), 2)})
by_sex = pd.DataFrame(rows)
by_sex["Level"] = pd.Categorical(by_sex.Level, LEVEL_ORDER, ordered=True)
show_table(by_sex.sort_values(["Year", "Level"]),
           "Caregiver-reported ASD by recorded sex, level and year: unweighted percentages of the records in each "
           "file, and the ratio between them with a log-delta 95% interval that assumes independent students",
           {"% males": 2, "% females": 2, "Ratio of the two percentages": 2})
ratios = by_sex.pivot_table(index="Level", columns="Year", values="Ratio of the two percentages", observed=True)
ratio_first, ratio_last = int(ratios.columns.min()), int(ratios.columns.max())
falling = int((ratios[ratio_last] < ratios[ratio_first]).sum())
# The item is not the same instrument in those years, so the direction is read against that, not past it.
names_per_year = items.loc[items.Year.isin(ratios.columns)].groupby("Year")["ASD variable"].nunique()
codes_per_year = {int(y): observed_codes(audit.loc[audit.year.eq(y)]) for y in ratios.columns}
note(f"The ratio of the two percentages falls between {ratio_first} and {ratio_last} in {falling} of the "
     f"{len(ratios)} levels, and is lowest in {ratios[ratio_last].idxmin().split(' (')[0]}, the oldest cohort. That "
     "direction cannot be separated from the instrument, which changes in every one of those years: the ASD item "
     "is carried by "
     + ", ".join(f"{int(n)} variable name" + ("s" if n > 1 else "") + f" in {int(y)}"
                 for y, n in names_per_year.items())
     + "; the values observed in the files are "
     + "; ".join(f"{codes} in {year}" for year, codes in codes_per_year.items())
     + f"; the filter question is reworded more than once; and {NO_WEIGHT_YEAR} publishes no expansion weight at "
       "all. The percentages here are unweighted in every year for that reason, which keeps them comparable in "
       "construction but not in wording. Read carefully, this is a statement about who a caregiver reports as "
       "diagnosed in a school survey, in cohorts that are not followed over time; it is not a change in any "
       "individual child and it is not comparable with the sex ratios of hospital episodes or programme entries, "
       "which count different events.")
```

## Quality and comparability

```{python}
#| label: tabla-educacion-calidad
breaks = pd.DataFrame([
    {"Record": "PIE (Apuntes 60)", "Year": DROP_YEAR, "Kind": "Denominator collapses and rebounds",

    {"Record": "PIE / SINACES", "Year": HANDOVER, "Kind": "Source change",
     "What changes": "The harmonised series passes from Apuntes 60 to the SINACES report; the strict and Asperger "
                     "split stops being published",
     "Effect on comparability": "Counts remain comparable in the overlap; the categorical split cannot be continued"},
    {"Record": "PIE / SINACES", "Year": HANDOVER, "Kind": "Denominator change",

     "Effect on comparability": "Shares before and after the switch are taken over different bases"},
    {"Record": "SINACES", "Year": LAST, "Kind": "Denominator falls",

                                f"{number(APPLICANT_SHARE_LAST, 1)}% autism share in {LAST} is the denominator "
                                "shrinking rather than the numerator growing"},

     "What changes": "The printed PIE figure and the total minus special schools differ by "
                     f"{number(abs(gap_years['Difference (SINACES − Apuntes 60)'].iloc[0]))} students",
     "Effect on comparability": "Resolved by an explicit rule; both values are kept in separate series"},

     "What changes": "Sex is published for one year only, in a third document",

    {"Record": "JUNAEB EVE", "Year": ITEM_FIRST_YEAR, "Kind": "Item appears",
     "What changes": "An autism category is added to the prolonged-condition checklist",
     "Effect on comparability": "Earlier years are not zeros; no series exists before this year"},
    {"Record": "JUNAEB EVE", "Year": NO_WEIGHT_YEAR, "Kind": "No published weight",
     "What changes": "The files carry no expansion factor",

     "What changes": f"The ASD variable in {blank_level} is blank for every record",

    {"Record": "JUNAEB EVE", "Year": int(junaeb.Year.max()), "Kind": "Response coding change",
     "What changes": "The checklist is coded 0/1 for every respondent who answers yes at the filter, instead of "

                     "never reached it",

show_table(breaks, "Every break in the education record over the period, what it changes, and what it costs in "
                   "comparability")
```

Five weaknesses are worth naming plainly, because every number above inherits at least one of them.

**The unit is a registration, not a person.** A student registered in PIE in two consecutive years is
two rows in two annual stocks. Nothing in the published aggregates permits following an individual,
and no figure here is a count of distinct persons over the period.

**The register measures eligibility and provision as much as recognition.** A registration requires a
diagnosis, but it also requires an establishment with a PIE, a professional to complete the
assessment, and either an available Decree 170 place or an exceptional authorisation. The rising
share of exceptional entries is direct evidence that the supply constraint binds. Growth in this
series therefore mixes clinical recognition, administrative capacity and the financial incentive
attached to the subsidy, in proportions the data cannot separate.

**The denominators do not match the numerators.** Total PIE enrolment counts students with any
special educational need in state-funded establishments; the population denominator counts residents
of all ages; the survey denominators count records in a file. None of them is the population of
school-age children in Chile, so none of the percentages on this page is a prevalence, and the shares
across the source switch are not taken over the same base.

```{python}
#| label: debilidad-missingness
#| output: asis
# The missingness weakness is not the same weakness in the two weighted years — it is large in the first
# and gone in the second — so it is stated year by year, from the audit rather than from memory.
blank_share = 100 * audit.n_item_blank_filter_yes / audit.n_filter_yesno_all
spread = audit.weighted_pct_complete_case - audit.weighted_pct_full
widths = pd.Series([float(edu.loc[row.year, f"junaeb_{row.level}_pct_weighted_hi"]
                          - edu.loc[row.year, f"junaeb_{row.level}_pct_weighted_lo"])
                    for row in audit.itertuples()], index=audit.index)
clauses = []
for survey_year in WEIGHTED_YEARS:
    in_year = audit.year.eq(survey_year)
    estimable = in_year & audit.weighted_pct_full.notna()
    exceeding = int((spread[estimable] > widths[estimable]).sum())
    # blank_share is taken over the ESTIMABLE levels only. A level whose item is empty for every record
    # is a defect of the file, not caregivers declining to answer, and pooling the two would attribute
    # a missing variable to respondent behaviour and inflate the upper bound.
    empty_levels = in_year & audit.n_item_nonempty.eq(0)
    if blank_share[estimable].max() > 0:
        opening = (f"In {survey_year} between {number(blank_share[estimable].min(), 1)}% and "
                   f"{number(blank_share[estimable].max(), 1)}% of the students whose caregiver reported a prolonged "
                   "condition left every checklist category blank")
        if empty_levels.any():
            named = ", ".join(LEVELS.get(l, l) for l in audit.level[empty_levels])
            opening += (f" (the {named} item is excluded from that range: it is empty for every record that "
                        "year, which is a defect of the file rather than a caregiver not answering)")
    else:
        opening = (f"In {survey_year} no student who answered the filter was left blank, because the checklist "
                   "carries an explicit 0 or 1 for everyone who reaches it")
    clauses.append(f"{opening}, and moving from the full file to the complete case moves the estimate by "
                   f"{number(spread[estimable].min(), 2)} to {number(spread[estimable].max(), 2)} percentage points "
                   f"against 95% intervals {number(widths[estimable].min(), 2)} to "
                   f"{number(widths[estimable].max(), 2)} points wide, with {exceeding} of the "
                   f"{int(estimable.sum())} moving by more than its own interval")
print(f"**The survey's missingness was larger than its uncertainty in {WEIGHTED_YEARS[0]}, and is gone by "
      f"{WEIGHTED_YEARS[-1]}.** " + ". ".join(clauses) + ". The two weighted years therefore carry different "
      "denominator risks and are not interchangeable. In both of them the interval itself is computed as though "
      "students were sampled independently, which they were not, so the comparison between the two flatters the "
      "interval in every year.")
```

**There is no geography, no age and no school.** No tracked education table carries a region, a
commune, an age, a grade within level or an establishment. The territorial analysis this report
performs on the hospital and community records cannot be repeated here, and the study's own
reproduction controls record the commune-level education check as unavailable rather than as passed.

# Synthesis

```{python}
#| label: sintesis
#| output: asis
first_h, last_h = harmonised.index.min(), harmonised.index.max()
main = pie_models.loc[pie_models.model_id.eq(f"pie_harmonised:none:{FIRST}-{LAST}")].iloc[0]
disruption = pie_models.loc[pie_models.model_id.eq(f"pie_harmonised:disruption:{FIRST}-{LAST}")].iloc[0]
last_junaeb = junaeb.loc[junaeb.Year.eq(junaeb.dropna(subset=["Weighted %"]).Year.max())].dropna(subset=["Weighted %"])
# How far each of the last year's estimates moves when the denominator changes, against how wide its own
# interval is. Both quantities come from the tables above; neither is asserted in the prose.
last_survey_year = int(last_junaeb.Year.iloc[0])
survey_audit = audit.loc[audit.year.eq(last_survey_year)].set_index("level")
denominator_shift = {}
for _, survey_row in last_junaeb.iterrows():
    audit_row = survey_audit.loc[LEVEL_KEYS[survey_row["Level"]]]
    denominator_shift[survey_row["Level"].split(" (")[0]] = (
        float(audit_row.weighted_pct_complete_case - audit_row.weighted_pct_full),
        float(survey_row["hi"] - survey_row["lo"]))
shift_values = [move for move, _ in denominator_shift.values()]
shift_widths = [width for _, width in denominator_shift.values()]
exceeding_levels = [name for name, (move, width) in denominator_shift.items() if move > width]
first_weighted = audit.loc[audit.year.eq(WEIGHT_FIRST_YEAR) & audit.weighted_pct_full.notna()]
first_shift = first_weighted.weighted_pct_complete_case - first_weighted.weighted_pct_full
first_widths = pd.Series([float(edu.loc[row.year, f"junaeb_{row.level}_pct_weighted_hi"]
                                - edu.loc[row.year, f"junaeb_{row.level}_pct_weighted_lo"])
                          for row in first_weighted.itertuples()], index=first_weighted.index)
first_multiple = first_shift / first_widths
bullets = [
    f"Students registered in PIE under an autism category rose from {number(harmonised.loc[first_h])} in "
    f"{int(first_h)} to {number(harmonised.loc[last_h])} in {int(last_h)}, a factor of "
    f"{number(harmonised.loc[last_h] / harmonised.loc[first_h], 1)}, with an average annual change of "
    f"{number(main.apc, 1)}% ({ci(main.apc_lo, main.apc_hi)}); adding an indicator for the disrupted "
    f"{FIRST + 1}–{FIRST + 2} school years leaves it at {number(disruption.apc, 1)}% "
    f"({ci(disruption.apc_lo, disruption.apc_hi)}). These are annual school-register stocks: what grew is "
    "recognition and registration inside the school system, not the occurrence of autism.",
    f"The two published definitions diverge: over {FIRST}–{LAST_APUNTES} the strict autism category grows at "
    f"{number(strict_model.apc, 1)}% a year against {number(asperger_model.apc, 1)}% for Autism–Asperger, so the "
    "harmonised sum is the only series that can be carried across the whole period, and a strict-only series would "
    "describe a coding migration as much as a change in recognition.",
    f"The series changes documents in {HANDOVER}. In the {len(overlap)} overlapping years the two sources agree to "
    f"within {number(abs(gap_years['Difference (SINACES − Apuntes 60)']).max())} students, but after the switch the "
    "categorical split is gone and the denominator becomes PIE applicants rather than PIE enrolment; in that source "
    "the count of autistic applicants equals the count of autistic students exactly, so demand and registration are "
    "not distinguished.",
    f"Autism reaches {number(APPLICANT_SHARE_LAST, 1)}% of all PIE applicants by {LAST}, over a denominator that "
    f"fell {number(abs(APPLICANT_DROP), 1)}% that year: {number(APPLICANT_SHARE_LAST - APPLICANT_SHARE_HELD, 2)} of "
    f"those {number(APPLICANT_SHARE_LAST, 1)} points are the denominator shrinking rather than the numerator "
    f"growing. {number(last_entry['% by exceptional entry'], 1)}% of autistic applicants "
    "enter by exceptional authorisation rather than through the programme's ordinary places — a supply constraint "
    "visible in the register itself. Special autism schools grow from "
    f"{number(special.loc[special_first, 'special_schools_autism'])} to "
    f"{number(special.loc[special_last, 'special_schools_autism'])} students and fall as a share of all autistic "
    "students in the education system.",
    f"The school survey supports a weighted estimate in only {len(WEIGHTED_YEARS)} of the {len(YEARS)} years and "
    "only for the levels in which the item was both asked and answered: "
    + "; ".join(f"{r['Level'].split(' (')[0]} {number(r['Weighted %'], 1)}% ({ci(r['lo'], r['hi'], 1)})"
                for _, r in last_junaeb.sort_values("Level").iterrows())
    + f" in {last_survey_year}. Every one of these is a percentage of the records in a school file, computed without "
      "strata, cluster or school identifier. Changing the denominator from the whole file to the complete case moves "
      f"them by {number(min(shift_values), 2)} to {number(max(shift_values), 2)} percentage points, against "
      f"intervals {number(min(shift_widths), 2)} to {number(max(shift_widths), 2)} points wide: "
    + (", ".join(exceeding_levels) + (" moves" if len(exceeding_levels) == 1 else " move")
       + " by more than its own interval and the rest do not"
       if exceeding_levels else "none moves by more than its own interval")
    + f". In {WEIGHT_FIRST_YEAR}, the other weighted year, the same change moved the estimate by "
      f"{number(first_shift.min(), 2)} to {number(first_shift.max(), 2)} points, "
      f"{number(first_multiple.min())} to {number(first_multiple.max())} times the width of the interval published "
      "beside it. None of these numbers is a prevalence.",
    "The education record has no geography, no age and no school, and publishes sex for a single year. It can say "
    "how many school registrations carry an autism category and under which rule; it cannot say where, at what age, "
    "to whom, or how many distinct children.",
]
for bullet in bullets:
    print(f"- {bullet}")
    print()
```

## Reproducibility

Every figure and table on this page is computed in the chunk that displays it, from tables tracked in
git: `docs/study/data/education_summary_year.csv`, `pie_source_provenance.csv`,
`junaeb_denominator_audit.csv`, `coverage_layers_year.csv` and `models_summary.csv`, together with the
published corpus tables `ST6_junaeb_items.csv`, `E76_education_pie_full.csv`,
`S12_junaeb_sex_level.csv` and `E79_reproduction_controls_by_family.csv`. That is the whole input list:
the chapter reads nothing it does not use, so `pie_enriched_context_verified.csv` and `fig3a_pie.csv`,
which restate the same PIE series in other shapes, are not loaded here and are not claimed as sources
of anything on the page. No value is transcribed by hand and nothing is read from a geospatial file,
because no tracked education table carries a region or a commune.

The prior extraction is documented in the provenance table itself: each published PIE, SINACES or
special-school value keeps the document it was read from, the physical page, the caption of the table
on that page, the definition recorded beside it and the SHA-256 of the file, and is flagged as
printed or as computed from printed cells. The survey side keeps the microdata file, its encoding,
its dictionary and questionnaire, the exact variable that carries the ASD item, the values observed
in it and the weight column, for every level and year. The growth models are read from
`models_summary.csv` with their residual degrees of freedom, dispersion and Durbin–Watson statistic
attached, so the weakness of a log-linear fit on seven points stays visible beside its interval.

The extension this source most needs is not more years but more columns: a regional and age breakdown
of the PIE register, a sex split published every year rather than once, an establishment count for
the special schools, and a survey file that publishes the sampling design alongside the weight. Until
then the education record can be counted accurately and cannot be disaggregated at all.
